key_insight: Machine learning models can quantify national-level "peace" signals from online news and social media, and those models can generalize across different news datasets; the work also pairs measurement with user-facing tools that help people understand and improve their media diets to foster peace.
problem_solved: Lack of scalable, data-driven methods to measure peace-related signals in media ecosystems and few practical tools that help users recognize how their media consumption may influence polarization and conflict dynamics.
method: Train neural networks on text embeddings from online news sources to predict a continuous measure of "peace"; validate transfer performance on a separate news dataset (high cross-dataset accuracy).
Apply comparable ML analysis to social media signals (e.g., platform content, comments, transcripts) to extend measurement beyond traditional news.
Deploy user-facing online tools that visualize a user's media diet and provide actionable feedback to reduce exposure to conflict-amplifying content.
impact: Provides a replicable pipeline for researchers and practitioners to measure peace metrics from heterogeneous media, test model generalization, and translate insights into actionable interventions that nudge healthier media consumption and reduce conflict amplification.
visual_elements: World map heatmap showing country-level peace scores derived from news and social media
Pipeline diagram: data sources → text embeddings → neural model → peace score → user dashboard
Side-by-side bar chart comparing model performance (accuracy/robustness) across original and transfer news datasets
Mockup of the online media-diet tool (timeline/traffic-light indicators and personalized recommendations)
paper_title: Measuring and Fostering Peace through Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
paper_authors: P. Gilda, P. Dungarwal, A. Thongkham, E. T. Ajayi, S. Choudhary
